subject: physiology
title: Spermatogenesis, Sertoli Cells, and Leydig Cell Regulation

steps.tx: Male reproductive function is anchored by the dual endocrine and gametogenic operations of the paired testes. Compartmentalized within convoluted seminiferous tubules, continuous production of haploid spermatozoa from diploid spermatogonia is designated **spermatogenesis**, requiring seventy-four days to complete full developmental maturation.
steps.say: Spermatogenesis takes seventy-four days within seminiferous tubules, producing haploid sperm from diploid precursors.

rows: Rapidly completes Meiosis II without delay
Condensed protamine nucleus; shed into tubule lumen

steps.tx: The somatic nurse cells of the seminiferous epithelium are the columnar **Sertoli cells**, extending from the basal lamina to the tubular lumen. Sertoli cells envelop developing germ cells, providing essential structural support, metabolic lactate nutrition, and phagocytosis of discarded spermatid residual cytoplasm.
steps.say: Sertoli cells act as nurse cells spanning the tubule, nourishing germ cells and engulfing discarded cytoplasm.

left.title: Sertoli Cells (Intratubular)
points: Target of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) via Gs/cAMP
Form the blood-testis barrier via tight junctions
Secrete Androgen-Binding Protein (ABP) and Inhibin B
Convert testosterone to estradiol via aromatase enzyme

right.title: Leydig Cells (Interstitial)
points: Located in vascular connective tissue outside tubules
Target of luteinizing hormone (LH) via Gs/cAMP
Synthesize and secrete over 95% of circulating testosterone

steps.tx: Adjacent Sertoli cells form specialized occluding zonula occludens tight junctions near the tubular basement membrane, establishing the impenetrable **blood-testis barrier**. This anatomical barrier divides the seminiferous epithelium into a basal compartment containing diploid spermatogonia and a specialized adluminal compartment housing developing post-meiotic spermatocytes.
steps.say: The blood-testis barrier isolates post-meiotic germ cells from the immune system using tight junctions between Sertoli cells.

nodes.label: Adjacent Sertoli Cell Basolateral Membranes Form Occluding Tight Junctions
Establishes Blood-Testis Barrier: Separates Basal from Adluminal Compartments
Post-Meiotic Spermatids Express Novel Haploid Cell-Surface Neo-Antigens
Prevents Autoimmune Recognition, Halting Cytotoxic Autoantibody Formation

steps.tx: Because meiotic recombination generates novel haploid cell-surface antigens that the host immune system would recognize as foreign, the blood-testis barrier creates **testicular immune privilege**. Breach of this barrier through testicular trauma, biopsy, or mumps orchitis permits autoantibody formation, causing secondary autoimmune infertility.
steps.say: Disrupting the blood-testis barrier allows autoimmune antibodies to form against sperm, causing infertility.

vis.caption: Seminiferous tubule cross-section, Sertoli-germ cell junctions, and interstitial Leydig clusters.

steps.tx: Endocrine regulation of testicular gametogenesis and steroidogenesis operates via the classic hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis. Hypothalamic gonadotropin-releasing hormone stimulates anterior pituitary gonadotrophs to secrete **luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone** in synchronized, pulsatile bursts every ninety to one hundred twenty minutes throughout adult life.
steps.say: Pulsatile hypothalamic GnRH drives pituitary release of LH to stimulate Leydig cells, and FSH to stimulate Sertoli cells.

nodes.label: Hypothalamic Arcuate Nucleus Emits Pulsatile GnRH Bursts Every 90-120 Minutes
Anterior Pituitary Gonadotrophs Secrete Glycoproteins LH and FSH
LH Binds Leydig Cells -> Stimulates Testosterone Synthesis
FSH Binds Sertoli Cells -> Drives Spermatogenesis and ABP Secretion

steps.tx: Luteinizing hormone acts on interstitial Leydig cells via cyclic AMP to stimulate the steroidogenic synthesis of **testosterone from cholesterol**. Over ninety-five percent of circulating male testosterone is produced by Leydig cells, while the remainder is contributed by the adrenal zona reticularis.
steps.say: Luteinizing hormone stimulates Leydig cells to produce ninety-five percent of circulating testosterone.

left.title: Systemic Circulating Testosterone
points: Normal male serum concentration: 300 to 1000 ng/dL
60% bound tightly to Sex Hormone-Binding Globulin (SHBG)
Only 2% circulates as free active hormone

right.title: Intratesticular Testosterone
points: Concentrated 100-fold higher than systemic blood levels
Tightly bound by Androgen-Binding Protein (ABP) in tubule fluid
Absolute requirement for normal spermatogenesis progression
Exogenous testosterone suppresses LH, paradoxically causing azoospermia

steps.tx: Sertoli cells synthesize and secrete the high-affinity glycoprotein **androgen-binding protein** into the tubular lumen under follicle-stimulating hormone stimulation. Androgen-binding protein sequesters testosterone, maintaining intratesticular testosterone concentrations one hundred times higher than systemic circulation, an absolute physiological requirement for normal spermatogenesis.
steps.say: Androgen-binding protein concentrates testosterone inside seminiferous tubules to levels one hundred times higher than blood.

vis.caption: Seminiferous germ cell kinetics, testicular endocrine tumors, and gonadotropic dysregulation.

steps.tx: Selective negative feedback on pituitary FSH secretion is exerted by the heterodimeric glycoprotein **inhibin B**, synthesized by Sertoli cells in proportion to active spermatogenesis. Conversely, circulating testosterone feeds back to both the hypothalamus and pituitary, suppressing pulsatile secretion of GnRH and luteinizing hormone.
steps.say: Inhibin B from Sertoli cells selectively suppresses FSH, while testosterone inhibits both LH and hypothalamic GnRH.

rows: Inhibits pulsatile GnRH and selectively suppresses LH
Selectively suppresses FSH secretion without altering LH
